scenarioStory.history: Sudden onset of substernal chest pressure approximately 40 minutes ago while mowing the lawn, described as "an elephant sitting on my chest," radiating to the jaw. Associated nausea, diaphoresis, and lightheadedness when he tried to stand. Denies similar prior episodes. Wife called 911 when he became pale and had to sit down.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 57-year-old male seated, pale, and diaphoretic with ongoing substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw. He is alert but visibly uncomfortable, with borderline low blood pressure on initial vitals. → 12-lead acquired and fluid bolus given: Crew acquires a 12-lead EKG showing inferior ST elevation with right-sided leads confirming RV involvement. Recognizing the hypotension as preload-dependent, the crew establishes IV access and gives a fluid bolus before nitrates. → BP responds, nitro given cautiously: Following fluid resuscitation, the patient's blood pressure improves enough to support cautious nitroglycerin administration. The crew continues serial vitals and transmits the STEMI alert while transporting to a PCI-capable facility.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw, lightheaded

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 57-year-old male seated, pale, and diaphoretic with ongoing substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw. He is alert but visibly uncomfortable, with borderline low blood pressure on initial vitals.
relatedChecklist: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes; transmit for STEMI interpretation
Establish IV access; if unable within 2 attempts or 90 seconds, place IO
500 mL NS bolus IV, pressure-infused over <15 min, reassess before repeating (up to 30 mL/kg = 2700 mL max)

scenarioEvents.name: 12-lead acquired and fluid bolus given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew acquires a 12-lead EKG showing inferior ST elevation with right-sided leads confirming RV involvement. Recognizing the hypotension as preload-dependent, the crew establishes IV access and gives a fluid bolus before nitrates.
relatedChecklist: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL once BP supports it; may repeat q3–5 min if SBP >100
Reassess vital signs and rhythm serially en route; repeat 12-lead if condition changes

scenarioEvents.name: BP responds, nitro given cautiously
scenarioEvents.description: Following fluid resuscitation, the patient's blood pressure improves enough to support cautious nitroglycerin administration. The crew continues serial vitals and transmits the STEMI alert while transporting to a PCI-capable facility.

scenarioEvents.name: Nitro given before fluid bolus
scenarioEvents.description: The crew administers sublingual nitroglycerin immediately per routine chest pain management without first correcting the patient's borderline hypotension. Given the preload-dependent RV infarct, blood pressure drops precipitously.
relatedChecklist: Rescue: 500 mL NS bolus IV immediately, pressure-infused, reassess for repeat
